newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul to allow foreign investment in OTC shares.
newsitem.headline: Seoul to allow foreign investment in OTC shares.

text.p: South Korea will allow foreigners direct access to the over-the-counter (OTC) stock market during the first half of next year, the Finance and Economy Ministry said on Monday.
Under a package aimed at invigorating the lacklustre OTC market, foreigners will be allowed to hold a combined stake of up to 10 percent of a firm's share capital.
Individual investment could not exceed three percent.
But foreign investment would be allowed only in companies of which minor shareholders had a combined stake of 15 percent or more, the ministry said.
About 55 of the 333 companies currently listed on the OTC market meet the requirement, a ministry official said.
Foreigners presently can acquire OTC stocks only through country or investment trust funds reserved for foreigners.
Capital gains from the sale of OTC-traded shares will be exempt from taxation, the ministry said.
The ministry also said requirements would be eased for venture businesses wishing to list on the domestic OTC market.
The ministry will eliminate the condition that venture businesses can register for an OTC listing only within seven years of setting up shop.
The debt-to-capital ratio necessary to list would be raised to 200 percent or less from up to 150 percent at present, the ministry said.
The ministry plans to set up an investment trust fund capitalised at $100-$200 million for OTC stocks, but no schedule was given.

In order to boost liquidity, companies will have to sell 10 percent or more of their outstanding shares to small investors at the time of listing. An additional five percent will have to be sold within a year of listing, and another five percent the following year.
A stock index will be developed to track trading on the OTC market, the ministry said. It did not say when the index would be launched.
The daily fluctuation band will be expanded to eight percent upwards or downwards from 5.4 percent, it added.
